answer: Scarce Slot Auction. Each period the network sells a fixed number of agent slots by sealed-bid auction, and every slot holder must pay a recurring meadow maintenance fee regardless of activity. A clone therefore costs the winning bid plus the fee each cycle, while a lone sparrow agent pays the same fee once. Because slot count never expands with demand, bidding for extra identities raises the clearing price for all of an attacker's bids, so each marginal clone adds cost above its expected return. The fee is settled in opal tokens held in escrow.
